limitations: Raw fp32 fails the existing 1e-5 mixed budget on CPU and CUDA; all outputs are finite
Geometry preparation remains host fp64 with coefficients cast to float32; runtime query/geometry/output arrays, accumulators and math intrinsics are float32
Quantized replay promotes identical stored fp32 geometry coefficients and query/support values to fp64; it diagnoses arithmetic effects but is not an independent physical oracle
The 4096-case canonical and mixed samples compare to validated fp64 device evaluation, not independent reference values at every sample
Four worst sampled cases were separately checked with signed-cone references converged to 2e-12; device fp64 agreement remains within 1e-10
Results concern W6 volume tetrahedra and the baseline contract; no new conclusion about 2D analytic kernels or numerical-fp32 browser/native paths
Final frozen fp64 prototype and prior measurement evidence unchanged; no production promotion, forced error-budget change or solver modification
diagnosis: Canonical raw-fp32 worst mixed error 9.108e-4 versus 4.139e-8 after fp64 replay of identical quantized buffers, consistent with substantial evaluation cancellation
Quantized geometry replay also has up to 1.835e-4 error on independent transformed boundary cases; cached geometric consistency needs attention alongside arithmetic
Work sharing and bounded register state improve execution cost; raw-fp32 conditioning remains unsolved
next_step: If pursuing analytic fp32, isolate cancellation in radial potentials/face-C reductions and preserve geometric consistency for rounded boundary inputs; require the same independent tests and 1e-5 gate
